messages:
incident-bot: Paging: High-severity - metering pipeline undercount detected for hosted API customers since ~2026-03-15T02:10Z. Rate of dropped events spiked to ~18% on consumer group metering-event-consumers. Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/metering-incident Tue
sophia (on-call): ack. I'm on it, looking at consumer logs now. assign to eng-sre.
sophia (on-call): `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/metering-consumer --since=1h | grep ERR` - seeing repeated DB unique constraint failures on write_batch_id
alex: jumping in. those unique constraint errs mean the write batch dedupe path is failing, consumer treating duplicate as fatal instead of acking. rolling restart of the consumer should mute the flood. doing canary restart on 1 pod.
alex: restarted pod metering-consumer-2, error rate dropped on that pod. still seeing backlog in kafka topic meter-events with ~120k messages.
mike (billing): quick question — customer-visible impact? invoices or dashboard numbers?
sophia (on-call): customer dashboards are showing LOWER usage than actual for a subset of customers (hosted tier) because events were dropped. invoices generated from nightly job at 04:00 UTC may miss those events -> potential underbilled invoices or delayed invoices if we choose to hold and reconcile.
priya (cs): flagged 3 enterprise customers already pinged via account reps asking why daily usage shows 0 for yesterday. they want ETA.
derek (product): we need a status page message asap. short and concrete. propose: "We are investigating an issue affecting usage metrics for some hosted customers. Some usage may not display in dashboards; invoices generated during the incident may be incomplete. We are working to reprocess missing events and will provide updates." thoughts?
elaine (support): can we include a rough ETA? customers keep escalating without ETA.
sophia (on-call): current plan: 1) stop consumer autoscaling to prevent repeated failures 2) patch dedupe logic (quick hotfix) 3) reprocess backlog with idempotent replay tool 4) run reconciliation, generate corrected invoices. expected timeline: hotfix + restart 30-45m; full reprocess 3-6h depending on backlog and tokenization. marking ETA for first customer-visible update: 60m.
alex: hotfix patched to treat duplicate batch write as ack and log. deploying to canary pool.
ops-bot: deploy-triggered: metering-consumer-hotfix -> canary -> success
alex: canary good, rolling deploy to remaining pods now.
ops-bot: deploy-success: metering-consumer-hotfix -> all pods
sophia (on-call): restarted ingestion and started reprocess job: `metering-reprocessor --topic meter-events --from-ts 2026-03-15T02:00Z --idempotent` monitoring reprocess speed now (approx 6k events/s).
priya (cs): drafting customer message for reps. here's a short template: "We detected a metering ingestion issue that caused some usage to not appear in dashboards. We are reprocessing data and will reconcile invoices. You will receive a follow-up with corrected invoices within 5 business days. We're prioritizing enterprise accounts now. Apologies for the disruption." need legal review?
derek (product): legal okay with that copy. add link to status page and support contact.
sophia (on-call): status page draft (post to https://status.redwood.ai): "Investigating: Metering ingestion issue affecting hosted customers. Some dashboards may show lower than actual usage; nightly invoices may be incomplete. We are reprocessing events and will provide updates every 60 minutes. Impact: subset of hosted customers. Mitigation: reprocessing underway; manual invoice reconciliation scheduled." approve?
elaine (support): approve. add note for customers who already paid: refunds or credit process will be available if needed.
mike (billing): operational note: do NOT auto-send corrected invoices until reconciliation complete. We'll generate an adjustments batch and tag invoices with reconciliation_id. Running SQL to find impacted accounts: `SELECT account_id, SUM(expected_tokens) - SUM(billed_tokens) AS delta FROM metering_reconciliation WHERE incident_tag = 'metering-2026-03-15' GROUP BY account_id HAVING delta<>0;` — this will produce final correction amounts.
alex: monitoring logs show reprocessor throughput improving. reprocess up to 55% now, backlog down to 54k messages.
sophia (on-call): handoff at 03:00 UTC to alex (eng-sre) — I'm taking a break, will be reachable but handing primary incident owner to alex. remaining tasks for next shift: 1) complete reprocess 2) validate reconciliation samples for top 10 customers 3) coordinate customer notifications for enterprise accounts 4) prepare internal postmortem draft
alex: got it. taking over. I'll post another update in 60m.
priya (cs): queueing enterprise comms: will send initial message to affected accounts with owner contact. template includes: - short summary - what we are doing - next steps - expected timeline - contact link
derek (product): internal comms snippet for leadership: "We experienced a metering ingestion bug causing under-reporting of hosted customer usage between 02:10 and 04:00 UTC on 2026-03-15. We have mitigated the ingestion error, are reprocessing events, and will reconcile invoices. No evidence of data exfiltration. Customer impact: inaccurate dashboards and potential invoice differences. Estimated resolution for reprocess: within 6 hours."
alex: update 04:05 UTC: reprocess complete for 80% of backlog, no data corruption found in reprocessed events. starting reconciliation runs now. sample check against enterprise account acct_9876 matched expected delta of +12,340 tokens.
mike (billing): I'll generate the adjustments batch and put invoices into hold. Creating ticket BILL-4521 for manual review.
ops-bot: incident-note: metering-2026-03-15 created, severity: high, owner: alex
alex: leaving final note before rotation: completed reprocess, reconciliation running, status page updated, CS notified. followups: postmortem, add better dedupe handling in next sprint, add alert on consumer duplicate error spikes.
priya (cs): thanks team. sending follow-up to affected enterprise accounts now. will also post to support queue template for small customers.
incident-bot: Incident update: Mitigation in progress. Next update at ~05:00 UTC or sooner if materially changed.
